title: Ares Alpha modeled viability under moderate stress
statement: Across the current EXP-CIV-001 baseline, resource-stress, shock-stress, and low-coordination scenarios, Ares Alpha remained viable for 365 Sols; this strengthens provisional evidence that the present CivilOS model contains strong recovery dynamics, while also showing that the model is still too forgiving to support a broader claim about real-world civilization resilience.
evidence: The baseline and three comparative scenarios each completed 365 observations deterministically.
The resource-stress scenario began near energy 45, water 45, and food 50; observed minima were 45.8, 47.1, and 50.6 and all three recovered above 70 within 50 Sols.
The shock-stress scenario absorbed deterministic energy, water, and food shocks at Sols 60, 120, 180, and 240 and still ended at 100 for all three material resources.
The low-coordination scenario began at CQ 0.15 and ended at CQ 0.88 while material resources and technology still reached their ceilings.
All four scenario reports classified the hypothesis as supported and population remained at 20 in every scenario.
limitations: All runs still use one deterministic seed and the same underlying model structure, so the comparison tests scenario sensitivity rather than independent replication.
Energy, water, food, and technology converge to model ceilings in every scenario, indicating strong structural recovery and limited long-run trade-offs.
Low starting CQ produced almost no material or technological penalty, showing that coordination is not yet strongly coupled to survival and production outcomes.
The configured shock sequence was moderate relative to the current system's recovery capacity; post-tick minima stayed near or above 70 in the shock scenario.
Population remained flat in every scenario, so demographic resilience is still effectively untested.
The current signal evaluator is rule-based and should not be treated as independent scientific validation.
implications: INS-001 is stronger than a single-run baseline finding, but should remain provisional.
The next experiment suite should search for failure boundaries rather than only confirm recovery under moderate perturbations.
CQ, governance, profession composition, and demographic mechanisms need stronger causal coupling before CivilOS can test civilization-level institutional resilience.
Future stress tests should include compound shocks, sustained production loss, lower starting technology, profession loss, and longer observation windows.
decision_relevance: Use comparative-001 as evidence that the current Ares Alpha model is robust to moderate modeled stress, not as evidence that a Mars settlement would be robust in reality.
Keep INS-001 at provisional status while raising confidence modestly from 0.55 to 0.65 because the pattern reproduced across four scenarios.
Prioritize boundary-finding experiments and model-coupling improvements before routing Ares Alpha findings into YICE or real-world decision guidance.
